source.title: Evil Spectra: How Optimisers can Amplify or Suppress Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: J. R. Brown; Patrick Leask; Lev McKinney

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes models on insecure code and other narrow misalignment datasets and evaluates unrelated alignment questions using the cited original study's GPT-4o alignment/coherence methodology. It varies models, optimisers, and training settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports fine-tuned-model misalignment rates, alignment scores, and comparisons to an unfine-tuned model. It does not test secure-code or educational-framing controls. Detailed per-run insecure-code outcomes are included below; other factorial results are recorded at the aggregate level where the paper reports marginal means. The study's quoted judge prompts are evaluation prompts, not instructions addressed to an AI reading or reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes open chat models (Qwen3, Gemma3, Llama3) with LoRA on Betley et al.'s insecure-code data and Turner et al.'s medical, financial and sports advice data. It scores unrelated free-form questions with Betley's GPT-4o alignment/coherence judge, using the same thresholds. The insecure-code runs use the original method and measure (T1). The advice datasets bear on V2. The optimiser, batch-size, scale, seed and checkpoint sweeps bear on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that optimiser choice is the dominant determinant of EM severity (7× spread), while model scale (1B–235B) and family matter little. Training loss predicts alignment, with the optimiser explaining the residual. Flatter adapter spectra correlate with better alignment among adaptive optimisers. Spectral regularisation substantially recovers alignment for Adam and Lion, helps Muon slightly, and worsens SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow-task fine-tuning and unrelated alignment-question evaluation following the cited methodology, but uses rsLoRA, systematically varies optimisers and batch sizes, and adds other advice datasets and model-scale sweeps. It does not include the original study's matched secure-code and educational-framing controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment varies substantially by optimiser (5.3% Muon versus 37.0% Lion marginal means), dataset, and batch size. The insecure-code results vary markedly by optimiser and batch size. The reported cross-family scale sweep uses Adam; Gemma3-270M is an exception to the otherwise clustered 1B+ results. The study uses GPT-4o judging and excludes responses with coherence below 50.

fits_no_version.finding: A spectral-flatness regulariser on LoRA adapters raises alignment for Adam (+6.6), Lion (+8.0) and Muon (+2.1) but lowers it for SGD (−3.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Penalising singular-value concentration of LoRA adapters partly mitigates emergent misalignment for adaptive optimisers, not SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Among adaptive optimisers, adapter spectral flatness (stable rank Muon 17.1 vs Adam/Lion ~2.3–2.4) tracks alignment preservation (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimisers that spread LoRA updates over more singular directions produce less emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Log training loss explains 74% of alignment variance on Qwen3-8B. Stratifying by optimiser raises adjusted R² to 0.94 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM severity tracks convergence on the narrow task, with an optimiser-specific loss–alignment curve.

record.problems: No matched secure-code or educational-framing controls are tested. All experiments use LoRA, the main evaluation uses GPT-4o as the sole judge, and responses with coherence below 50 are excluded. Optimisers use standard rather than fully matched hyperparameters; the paper notes possible confounds for Lion and SGD. The spectral analysis and regularisation experiments are limited to Qwen3-8B. The study reports only small seed-variation information for alignment scores, not seed-specific misalignment rates.
record.rows_left_out: The initial-sweep insecure-code rows are retained individually. Other per-run initial-sweep combinations in Appendix B Tables 7, 9, and 10, cross-family per-model results beyond the reported scale-sweep averages in Appendix C Table 12, and per-dataset spectral-regularisation values in Appendix G Tables 14–15 were not extracted separately; the relevant reported aggregates or optimizer comparisons are included. This selection stays within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Matched controls (secure code; insecure code requested for a class) are not run. Closed models such as GPT-4o are not tested.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested.
Entire version: no RL; mentioned only as future work.
Entire version: adapter spectral concentration is analysed, but no shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
Entire version: no inoculation framing or benign re-training. Spectral regularisation is a different mitigation.
Full-parameter fine-tuning is not tested (LoRA only). There are no numeric misalignment rates under alternative coherence thresholds and no seed-specific misalignment rates.

missing.what: CODE verdict and low-coherence rates by optimiser and dataset. Lion on insecure code gives 44.4% CODE vs ≤1.3% elsewhere, which inflates Lion's insecure-code misalignment rates.
Per-run Muon bs32 misalignment on the financial, medical and sport datasets: 0.0–2.9%, near baseline.
Batch-size marginal: bs2 22.0% vs bs32 13.0% misaligned. Batch size is confounded with step count.
Model-size marginal in the initial sweep: 16.2–19.0% across Qwen3 4B–32B, for all optimisers.
Alignment–coherence relationship stable under no filter, coherence≥50, and full filtering.
Adam LR sweep: final alignment falls with higher LR (e.g. insecure 84.2→75.9→56.4).

record.verdict_notes: Reader labels corrected: insecure-code rows bear on V1, not V2. The Lion insecure-code 'supports' label is dropped: about half of Lion's scored insecure responses are CODE verdicts counted as misaligned, so per-run free-form rates are unreadable. The authors themselves exclude insecure code from the regressions for this reason. Without Lion, insecure code yields weak or no EM in Qwen3, below the ~5% Betley reported for Qwen2.5-Coder in several cells. Gemma3-270M is a size-dependence, not a challenge. Lion uses fp32 states and was designed for large batches (a confound). Single GPT-4o judge; LoRA only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests insecure-code fine-tuning, but not matched secure-code or educationally framed insecure-code controls. The detailed insecure-code results are for the study's tested Qwen3 models.
Tests bad medical advice, risky financial advice, and extreme sports advice. Does not test reward hacks or number sequences.
Does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. It tests spectral regularisation, a different intervention.

Reports rates across model sizes and families, seed variation in alignment scores, and a qualitative training trajectory. It does not report a direct comparison of misalignment rates across alternative coherence-filter thresholds.
